text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) which won the parliamentary elections on Saturday is expected to start talks with the other parliamentary parties on the principles of the country's government, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said.
-- Bulgaria has gold deposits worth some $20 billion in its western Chelopech region, U.S. analyst Richard Rahn told the national radio. @
-- Bulgaria had a $43.4 million trade surplus with Asian countries last year, private Balkan agency said quoting Trade ministry figures.
-- Bulgaria's interim government is expected to discuss today a project for a new 20,000-lev note, which could be put in circulation in June, the government press centre said.
-- The Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA) is expected to discuss Bulgaria's application to join on September 12, Bulgaria's Trade ministry officials said.
-- Bulgaria's cartaker cabinet is expected to approve today a proposal to lift price controls as part of structural reform package agreed with international lenders.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency has received offers from 80 big foreign banks and firms for advisory services on the sale of 20-30 state-owned companies, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said. @

-- Bulgaria's canned food exports to Russia may rise four times under an intergovernmental accord for deliveries of Russian natural gas against Bulgarian commodities, Alexander Yotzev, executive director of the state Bulgarplod fruit and vegetable trader said.
-- Japan was ready to extend some $80 million for the modernisation of the Sofia airport, airport's executive director Danyo Adanev said.
-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) which won the parliamentary elections on Saturday was expected to name its nominee for a new prime minister on Thursday.
-- Bulgaria yesterday raised passenger railway fares by 58 percent in line with pledges made to multilateral lenders. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
